title: CASE OF WALLOVÁ AND WALLA v. THE CZECH REPUBLIC - [English Translation] by European Roma Rights Centre "ERRC"
conclusion: Remainder inadmissible;Violation of Art. 8;Not necessary to examine Art. 14;Non-pecuniary damage - financial award
summary: In the case of Wallová and Walla v. the Czech Republic, the applicants, a married couple of Roma origin, brought a complaint against the Czech state after their five children were removed from their care. The case highlighted the vulnerability of Roma and Traveller families who, due to poverty and inadequate housing, face disproportionate state intervention in family life. In September 2000, Czech authorities placed the Wallová and Walla children under supervision, citing the family’s lack of adequate accommodation. Despite the parents’ efforts to improve their situation, including attempts to secure housing and employment, the courts ordered the children’s provisional and later permanent placement in care institutions. The authorities justified these measures by pointing to the parents’ inability to provide suitable living conditions, but the applicants argued that the state failed to offer sufficient support to help them overcome their material difficulties. The European Court of Human Rights examined the case under Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life) and found a violation, ruling that the removal of the children was not a proportionate response to the family’s poverty and that less intrusive measures should have been considered. The Court awarded the applicants non-pecuniary damages. This judgment is significant as it underscores the need for states to support, rather than penalise, Roma and Traveller families facing social and economic hardship—a recurring issue in Europe’s recent history.
